source.original_text: Faithful ASTIS paraphrase of one component of Chen--Chewi--Lu--Zhang arXiv:2609.38710v1 Lemma 6.3, not quoted prose: after imposing a deterministic call cap, order the adjacent hybrids so that successive laws differ at only one call slot. For each fixed measurable final event, the absolute difference between the endpoint event probabilities is bounded by the sum of the absolute differences for adjacent hybrids, hence by the sum of their per-slot error budgets. This finite telescope does not prove the per-slot bounds or the separate capped-versus-uncapped error.

lean.statement: For real sequences a and δ and a natural number n, if every i<n satisfies |a (i+1) - a i| ≤ δ i, then |a n - a 0| ≤ ∑ i in Finset.range n, δ i.

blind_reconstruction.text: For every pair of real sequences a, delta : N -> R and every natural number n, if |a(i+1) - a(i)| <= delta(i) for every natural number i with i < n, then |a(n) - a(0)| <= sum_(i=0)^(n-1) delta(i). The sum is finite and ranges over precisely the indices 0 through n-1; for n = 0 it is the empty sum 0 and the conclusion is 0 <= 0. No condition is imposed on delta outside this index range, and no separate nonnegativity assumption is required.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.KernelTotalVariation

/-!
# Mean conditional-kernel errors and finite hybrid telescopes

This module isolates the reusable probability-kernel core of Chen--Chewi--Lu--
Zhang, arXiv:2609.38710v1, Lemma 6.3.  If two conditional Markov kernels differ
eventwise by an integrable history-dependent bound, their output laws differ by
at most the mean of that bound.  A common downstream Markov kernel preserves
the same estimate, so later adaptive computation is absorbed by data
processing.  A finite real-valued telescope then adds the adjacent hybrid
errors.

The declarations do not construct the paper's dummy-filled history kernels,
identify its `δ_t` with a measurable total-variation function, or compare the
capped ideal algorithm with its uncapped version.  Those adapters remain
separate source obligations.
-/

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Set Finset
open scoped ProbabilityTheory BigOperators

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.KernelHybridTelescope

/-- An integrable pointwise event bound between two Markov kernels controls the
corresponding event discrepancy after averaging over the input law.  This is
the mean-replacement step in the adaptive hybrid argument. -/
theorem abs_real_comp_sub_le_integral_eventBound
    {A B : Type*} [MeasurableSpace A] [MeasurableSpace B]
    (μ : Measure A) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (K L : Kernel A B) [IsMarkovKernel K] [IsMarkovKernel L]
    (ε : A → ℝ) (hε : Integrable ε μ)
    (hbound : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ s, MeasurableSet s →
      |(K x).real s - (L x).real s| ≤ ε x) :
    ∀ t, MeasurableSet t →
      |(K ∘ₘ μ).real t - (L ∘ₘ μ).real t| ≤ ∫ x, ε x ∂μ := by
  intro t ht
  have hint (M : Kernel A B) [IsMarkovKernel M] :
      Integrable (fun x => (M x).real t) μ := by
    apply (integrable_const (1 : ℝ)).mono'
      (M.measurable_coe ht).ennreal_toReal.aestronglyMeasurable
    exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x => by
      rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg ENNReal.toReal_nonneg]
      exact (measureReal_le_one : (M x).real t ≤ 1)
  have happly (M : Kernel A B) [IsMarkovKernel M] :
      (M ∘ₘ μ).real t = ∫ x, (M x).real t ∂μ := by
    change (Measure.bind μ M t).toReal = ∫ x, (M x t).toReal ∂μ
    rw [Measure.bind_apply ht M.aemeasurable]
    exact (integral_toReal (M.measurable_coe ht).aemeasurable
      (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x => measure_lt_top (M x) t)).symm
  rw [happly K, happly L, ← integral_sub (hint K) (hint L)]
  exact abs_integral_le_integral_abs.trans <|
    integral_mono_ae ((hint K).sub (hint L)).abs hε <|
      hbound.mono fun x hx => hx t ht

/-- The same mean replacement bound survives a common downstream Markov
kernel.  In an adjacent adaptive hybrid, the downstream kernel represents all
later calls after the one conditional rule being replaced. -/
theorem abs_real_comp_commonSuffix_sub_le_integral_eventBound
    {A B C : Type*} [MeasurableSpace A] [MeasurableSpace B] [MeasurableSpace C]
    (μ : Measure A) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (K L : Kernel A B) [IsMarkovKernel K] [IsMarkovKernel L]
    (S : Kernel B C) [IsMarkovKernel S]
    (ε : A → ℝ) (hε : Integrable ε μ)
    (hbound : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ s, MeasurableSet s →
      |(K x).real s - (L x).real s| ≤ ε x) :
    ∀ t, MeasurableSet t →
      |((S ∘ₖ K) ∘ₘ μ).real t - ((S ∘ₖ L) ∘ₘ μ).real t| ≤
        ∫ x, ε x ∂μ := by
  have hKL := abs_real_comp_sub_le_integral_eventBound μ K L ε hε hbound
  have hS := KernelTotalVariation.abs_real_comp_sub_le
    (K ∘ₘ μ) (L ∘ₘ μ) S hKL
  simpa only [← Measure.comp_assoc] using hS

/-- Finite adjacent-hybrid errors telescope.  Applying this to the output laws
of hybrids `0, ..., n` turns the one-slot bounds into their accumulated error.
The result is deliberately stated for real sequences so it does not invent a
second total-variation definition. -/
theorem abs_sub_zero_le_sum_range_of_adjacent
    (a δ : ℕ → ℝ) (n : ℕ)
    (hstep : ∀ i < n, |a (i + 1) - a i| ≤ δ i) :
    |a n - a 0| ≤ ∑ i ∈ range n, δ i := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih =>
      calc
        |a (n + 1) - a 0| ≤ |a (n + 1) - a n| + |a n - a 0| := by
          exact abs_sub_le _ _ _
        _ ≤ δ n + ∑ i ∈ range n, δ i :=
          add_le_add (hstep n (Nat.lt_succ_self n))
            (ih fun i hi => hstep i (hi.trans (Nat.lt_succ_self n)))
        _ = ∑ i ∈ range (n + 1), δ i := by
          rw [sum_range_succ, add_comm]

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.KernelHybridTelescope

source.attribution: The adaptive sampler and Lemma 6.3 are due to Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu and Matthew S. Zhang. The explicit measurable-kernel decomposition is ASTIS's rigorous supporting expansion; no author endorsement is implied.

candidate_publication_context.statement: For a capped adaptive algorithm represented on a common dummy-filled history space, replacing one conditional kernel at a time changes the final output law by at most the ideal-history expectation of that call's conditional total-variation error. Summing adjacent hybrids gives the total capped implementation error; a separate capped-versus-uncapped comparison contributes epsilon_cap exactly once.
assumptions: All capped histories and conditional transitions are measurable and use genuine Markov probability kernels.
The ideal and implemented algorithms share a deterministic call cap and dummy continuation convention.
Each local conditional event discrepancy is bounded by an integrable history-dependent budget under the ideal pre-call history law.
The capped ideal output is compared separately with the uncapped ideal algorithm.

obligations.label: Average an almost-everywhere conditional event bound under the ideal history law
Apply the same downstream Markov continuation after one replaced call
Sum adjacent hybrid event discrepancies over the deterministic cap
Construct measurable dummy-filled histories and identify the paper's delta_t
Compare capped and uncapped ideal outputs and add epsilon_cap once

lesson.title: Finite adjacent hybrid errors add
lesson.statement: For real sequences a and δ and a natural number n, if every adjacent difference |a(i+1)−a(i)| is at most δ(i) for i<n, then the endpoint difference |a(n)−a(0)| is at most the sum of those n budgets.
assumptions: The hybrid chain has a fixed finite length n; this theorem says nothing about a random or infinite number of calls.
Each adjacent discrepancy is a real number with the displayed bound. In the paper consumer, a_i is the probability of one fixed output event under hybrid i.
The same event is followed through the whole telescope before taking a total-variation supremum.

steps.title: Split the last endpoint difference
steps.text: Insert the penultimate value a_n between a_{n+1} and a_0. The real triangle inequality separates the newest replacement error from the accumulated earlier error.
steps.lean: abs_sub_le is the triangle inequality in the required three-point form.

steps.title: Apply the newest budget and the induction hypothesis
steps.text: The step assumption bounds the first term by δ_n. The induction hypothesis bounds the second by the sum through n−1. Appending δ_n gives exactly the finite range sum through n.
steps.lean: add_le_add combines the two bounds; Finset.sum_range_succ and commutativity identify the resulting expression with the canonical range sum.

lesson.lean_statement: This small real theorem is intentionally separate from probability-kernel definitions: it can telescope event discrepancies produced by any adjacent-hybrid construction without inventing another total-variation object.
lesson.lean_proof: Induction on n, one application of the three-point absolute-value inequality, and the finite range-sum recursion.
